Cloudflare Just Dropped 15% in a Week: Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up? ©teteescape and Alesia Kozik from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Cloudflare stock fell 15% in the past week (through Monday's close), while the Nasdaq 100 fell 3.7%.

The company put out no bad news, and the drop looks like a better entry point into a business that's still growing fast.

A sell-off in AI and richly valued software stocks hit Cloudflare, Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike, and at about 200x forward earnings Cloudflare is still expensive.

Third-quarter results come after the close on Nov. 5, and the consensus price target sits about 15% above Monday's close.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) stock is down 15% in the past week (through Monday's close). That leaves it nearly 20% below the record high it hit on Oct. 6. The Nasdaq 100 lost 3.7% over the same stretch.

Even so, Cloudflare is still up 51% in 2026.

A bad week for anything priced for AI

Three sessions did almost all the damage: Cloudflare fell 6.7% on Oct. 14, 2.5% on Oct. 15 and 6.3% on Oct. 16, as inflation worries and rising bond yields sent investors out of AI names and richly valued software.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW:NASDAQ) fell 14.1% and CrowdStrike (CRWD:NASDAQ) 13.3% over the same week. Cloudflare fell more than either Palo Alto or CrowdStrike, and it had the most to lose. At about 200x forward earnings, most of what buyers pay for sits years out, and higher yields make those years worth less today.

The company gave nobody a reason to sell

Cloudflare agreed to buy Deno to improve its Workers programming model. On Monday it also expanded the partner lineup for Cloudflare OS, its AI workspace.

Analysts kept raising their targets, too: BTIG, Oppenheimer, Barclays and TD Cowen lifted theirs between Oct. 6 and Oct. 13, to between $375 and $430.

As SaaStr founder Jason Lemkin put it on the 20VC podcast on Oct. 15: "They beat the quarter. They've accelerated growth even more." Second-quarter revenue rose 36% to $696.1 million.

Nov. 5 is the next test

Cloudflare reports third-quarter results after the close on Thursday, Nov. 5. Management guided for $736.0 million to $737.0 million of revenue, and Oppenheimer expects Cloudflare to beat that as more customers adopt its security products.

Analysts expect revenue to grow 32% this year, to $2.87 billion, and another 29% in 2027.

Cloudflare (NET): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024–2029 (TIKR)

That 2026 estimate is already at the top of management's full-year range, so Cloudflare needs a beat on Nov. 5.

Cheaper, but still not cheap

At about 200x forward earnings, Cloudflare is still expensive. But the Street's consensus target kept climbing into the drop.

Cloudflare (NET): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

At $343, the target sits about 15% above Monday's close.

title: Micron Just Dropped 10% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
detail:
Micron Just Dropped 10% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
Roxanna Maglangit

MU
SKHY
^NDX
Trade MU on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Micron Just Dropped 10% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up? ©Oleksii Mach and StreetOnCamara from Streetoncamara via Canva
Key Takeaways

Micron stock fell 10.9% in the past month through Monday's close, all of it after Oct. 7, as chip stocks sold off on fears about China's memory makers and about AI spending.

The selloff looks like a buying opportunity, because Micron's business and its earnings estimates kept climbing through it.

Micron guided to $61.5 billion of revenue for its fiscal first quarter, after a fiscal fourth quarter with an 86.8% gross margin.

The stock trades at about 5x fiscal 2027 earnings estimates, and the risk to watch is China's CXMT ramping up competitive memory by 2028.

Micron Technology (MU:NASDAQ) stock is down 10.9% in the past month (through Monday's close), while the Nasdaq 100 slipped just 0.4%. Fellow memory maker SK hynix (SKHY:NASDAQ) fell even harder, down 23.8%.

That's quite a reversal for a stock still up 217% in 2026 after a record quarter on Sept. 30. And all of the damage came after Oct. 7.

What exactly happened

Micron fell 4.8% on Oct. 8, when its only news was a strike vote by its Taiwan workers.

Then over the weekend, China's CXMT said it had made progress on a denser DRAM design and aims to launch server memory using it by the end of 2026. Micron dropped 3.9% on Oct. 12 and about 4% more the next day, while SK hynix sank 10.1% in Seoul.

A hotter-than-expected September CPI print knocked the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 4.3% on Oct. 14, and Micron fell 4.1%. Then on Friday, Oct. 16, Micron's worst day (-5.6%), worries about how all that AI spending gets financed hit chip stocks across the board.

Micron bounced about 3% on Monday with other chip stocks, with no news of its own.

China is going after Micron's best margins

Midday Friday, Elon Musk put a timeline on the China fear in a reply on X:

"For sure in 2027, but if China ramps LP5 & LP6 as fast as they've ramped other manufactured products, then 2028 will be a different story. HBM is a tougher hill to climb, however."

That's the right worry, because memory has never been more profitable for Micron. Its gross margin went from 2.7% in fiscal 2023 to 39.8% in fiscal 2025…

Micron Technology (MU): gross margin (%), fiscal 2021–2025 (years to August) (TIKR)

…then hit 80.7% in fiscal 2026, and 86.8% in the fourth quarter alone. Margins like that last only while memory stays scarce. (Fiscal 2023 shows what happens when it doesn't.)

For now, it's scarce. Bloomberg Intelligence's Vasu Kasibhotla said on Oct. 15 that the memory makers "all sold out capacity in 27 and probably a lot of 28 as well."

Micron's own numbers keep climbing

None of this has hurt the business. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue was $54.23 billion, nearly five times the year before, with $33.20 billion of adjusted free cash flow. Micron guided the current quarter to $61.5 billion of revenue, and CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said "we expect an even stronger fiscal 2027."

Oklo and NuScale Sink 15% in a Week: Is the Nuclear Selling Overdone? ©Kyle Miller from Pexels and Lerbank-bbk22 from Lerbank-bbk22 via Canva
Key Takeaways

Oklo stock fell 15% in the past week (through Monday's close) to a new 52-week low. NuScale Power fell 15% over the same week.

The biggest drop came on Oct. 14, when a hot September inflation report pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.26% and hit nuclear stocks far harder than the market.

Analysts expect about $6.5 billion more cash burn through 2030, more than twice Oklo's $3.0 billion of cash at June 30, so paying for the build is the main risk.

The third-quarter report in November and a definitive Centrus fuel deal are the next things to watch.

Oklo (OKLO:NYSE) stock is down 15.4% in the past week (through Monday's close), to a fresh 52-week low. NuScale Power (SMR:NYSE) fell 15.1% over the same stretch. The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.7%.

And almost none of it came from anything Oklo did.

Rates hit the nuclear trade hardest

Most of the damage came on Wednesday, Oct. 14. September's inflation report came in hotter than expected, the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.26%, and Oklo fell 8.6% while NuScale dropped about 10%.

That's the catch with companies whose profits are years away: with bonds paying 5%-plus, those profits are worth less today.

Friday took another 6.8% with no Oklo news behind it, wiping out Thursday's 3.3% bounce. Monday's 3% slip had no news behind it either, and Centrus Energy (LEU:NYSE) fell 4% with it.

Even good news didn't help. The stock kept sliding after the Department of Energy picked Oklo's Groves 2 isotope facility for its Nuclear Energy Launch Pad on Oct. 13.

The funding bill is still there

The bigger question is who pays for the build. Analysts expect Oklo to burn roughly $6.5 billion more through 2030. That's more than its $5.1 billion market value.

And at June 30, it held $3.0 billion of cash and marketable securities.

Sales won't close the gap soon: analysts expect just $8.9 million of revenue in 2027 and $122 million in 2029.

Oklo (OKLO): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2026–2029 (TIKR)

CFO Craig Bealmear said in August that two customers have already paid into the build. Until that money covers more of the bill, stock sales do the work, starting with a $1 billion at-the-market program signed on Sept. 11. At Monday's close, selling all of it would mean issuing about a fifth of the company.

Q3 is the real test

The mean price target has slid to $75, from about $89 at June 30 and a peak near $117 in January.

Oklo (OKLO): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

On Monday, Piper Sandler cut its target to $49 from $55 and kept its Overweight rating. Even the lower target is about 80% above Monday's close.

My take: On the news, the selling looks overdone. But every leg down makes Oklo's next stock sale cost shareholders more, so I'd wait for customer money to carry more of the build before buying.

Key Takeaways

Astera Labs fell 11.6% in the past week (through Monday's close). It had no news of its own, and worries about inflation and AI debt hit chip stocks.

Stifel kept its Buy rating and $460 price target through the drop, about 60% above Monday's close.

Second-quarter free cash flow fell by about half from a year earlier even as revenue forecasts kept rising, and that's the main risk.

At about 51x forward earnings, the stock trades well below its one-year average, and third-quarter results on Nov. 3 need to show cash catching up.

Astera Labs (ALAB:NASDAQ) lost 11.6% in the past week (through Monday's close). That's roughly three times the Nasdaq 100's 3.7% drop, and Astera put out no news.

The stock is now 43% below its 52-week high, though it's still up 72% in 2026.

Astera didn't give anyone a reason to sell

The slide started just before the week did. Astera fell 9% on Oct. 8 after a [Financial Times report](LINK NEEDED) put OpenAI's revenue below estimates, and Northland downgraded it to Market Perform on valuation the next morning.

Then two sessions did most of the damage. On Wednesday, Oct. 14, a hot inflation report raised bets on Fed rate hikes. A benchmark chip index fell 4.3%, and Astera dropped 7.7%. Marvell (MRVL:NASDAQ) fell 8.7% the same day.

On Friday, worries about AI debt at the neoclouds knocked 2.14% off the Nasdaq Composite, and Astera lost another 5.3%.

Over the week, Marvell fell 11% and Credo Technology (CRDO:NASDAQ) 14%. Credo fell even more than Astera, so this was a sector sell-off, and a stock with a five-year beta near 4 takes those hard.

Stifel isn't flinching

Stifel's Tore Svanberg kept his Buy rating and $460 price target on Friday, the day of the second drop. That's about 60% above Monday's close, and above the $388 consensus target.

The forecasts are moving his way. Consensus 2026 revenue has risen 23% since June 30, to $1.91 billion, with $2.98 billion expected in 2027.

Astera Labs (ALAB): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024–2029 (TIKR)
Cash flow has to catch up

The catch is cash. Second-quarter free cash flow was $67.2 million, about half the year before and well short of what analysts expected. It was flat with the first quarter even as revenue grew 27%.

Here's what's next

Astera reports third-quarter results after the close on Tuesday, Nov. 3. Management guided to $540 million to $560 million of revenue, and free cash flow needs to land clearly above the second quarter's. Samples of Aries 7, its new PCIe 7 chips, follow in the fourth quarter.

The stock also got cheaper: 50.9x forward earnings on Friday, down from about 62x on Oct. 8 and well below its 73.9x average over the past year.

Key Takeaways

AST SpaceMobile fell 18.6% in the past week (through Monday's close) after Piper Sandler downgraded it to Neutral and cut its target to $54 from $98.

Roth MKM kept its Buy rating and $108 target on Monday, well above the Street's $74 consensus target.

The stock trades well below its five-year average forward sales multiple, but loss estimates are widening and the satellite build is burning more than $1 billion a year.

Roth's call is plausible but stretched, and the FCC's Oct. 29 meeting and the launch of BlueBirds 14 to 16 are the next tests.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ) is down 18.6% in the past week (through Monday's close), while the Nasdaq 100 fell 3.7%. It's down 42.4% in 2026.

Yet Roth MKM kept its Buy rating and $108 target on Monday, 158% above that close.

Piper Sandler pulled the rug

On Oct. 9, SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) agreed to buy 800 MHz spectrum, and AST sank to what was then a 52-week low. The following Monday, Deutsche Bank upgraded AST to Buy. It argued that AST's spectrum covers nearly all of its enterprise value, and that SpaceX's push makes AST a more valuable partner for carriers.

That lasted one session. Before Tuesday's open, Piper Sandler cut AST to Neutral and its target to $54 from $98. It cited less conviction in the pace of AST's launches, plus competition from SpaceX. The stock fell 8.5% Tuesday, 10.5% Wednesday, and 8.6% Friday with no company news.

On Monday, four of AST's European carrier partners signed a letter of intent to explore a joint bid for satellite spectrum. That won back only part of the drop.

Roth's $108 rests on the launch schedule

Roth set its $108 target earlier this year. At the time it said the planned launches had AST on track for commercial service in late 2026, with 2027 sales approaching $1 billion. Launch pace is exactly what Piper lost faith in.

The rest of the Street is far more cautious.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

The consensus target rose from $54 to $74 over the past year, even as the stock more than halved.

AST does look cheap against its own history.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): forward (NTM) price/sales, last 5 years (TIKR)

It traded at 39.1x forward sales at Friday's close, against a five-year average of 60.3x. But $108 works out to over 100x those sales.

And losses are moving the wrong way. Over the 90 days to Oct. 12, the consensus 2026 loss widened from $1.51 a share to $2.28. The satellite build also burned more cash last year than in the four years before it combined.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): free cash flow, $ millions, fiscal 2021–2025 (TIKR)

Wall Street expects about $3.2 billion more burn before 2029, against more than $3.7 billion of pro forma cash at June 30. That's not much cushion if launches slip.

title: SK hynix Sinks 11% in a Week. Elon Musk: “HBM Is a Tougher Hill to Climb”
detail:
SK hynix Sinks 11% in a Week. Elon Musk: “HBM Is a Tougher Hill to Climb”
Bobby Sankhagowit
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:18 AM MST 5 min read
SKHY
^NDX
688825.SS
SK hynix Sinks 11% in a Week. Elon Musk: "HBM Is a Tougher Hill to Climb" ©mmac72 from Getty Images Signature and Corina Ciocirlan's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

SK hynix stock fell 11.9% in the past week (through Monday's close) after China's CXMT claimed a denser DRAM design and a Friday scare over AI debt hit chip stocks.

Elon Musk said a fast Chinese ramp in low-power memory could change things in 2028, but that HBM is a tougher hill to climb.

SK hynix's Seoul shares trade at about 3x forward earnings, less than half their five-year average of about 7x, and the US shares sit near 4x 2027 estimates, so the stock already prices in a downturn.

The third-quarter call on Oct. 28 is the next test, and firm customer commitments for 2027 would back the case for buying.

SK hynix (SKHY:NASDAQ) stock fell 11.9% in the past week (through Monday's close). That's more than three times the Nasdaq 100's 3.7% drop. And it came after a 4.7% bounce on Monday alongside Micron (MU:NASDAQ) and the other memory stocks.

A China scare and an AI-debt scare hit back to back. In the middle of it, Elon Musk posted a warning that reads better for SK hynix than the sell-off does.

China Lit the Fuse

On Oct. 10, the president of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) said its denser "4F²" DRAM design would go into server memory by the end of 2026. Nobody has verified the claim yet.

Seoul took it harder. SK hynix closed down 10.09% there on Tuesday, and the Kospi triggered its first sell-side trading curb in nearly two months. The US shares lost 3.2%.

Wednesday was worse: down 6.1%, as hot inflation data lifted bets on another Fed rate hike. Overnight, Korea's DealSite had reported that some of SK hynix's HBM4 back-end equipment orders may slip into next year. SK hynix told DealSite its investment is on schedule. The generous reading: SK hynix is reportedly shifting spending toward regular DRAM, where prices are rising. The less generous one is that HBM4 has hit a snag.

Then the AI Debt Scare Hit

Friday did the most damage. SK hynix fell 6.6% on fears that debt-laden AI data center builders can't earn enough to pay back what they've borrowed. The Nasdaq fell 2.14%, chip stocks posted an eighth straight losing day, and Micron lost 5.6%.

CoreWeave (CRWV:NASDAQ), the poster child for those worries, sank 12% that day, capping a 25% weekly drop. If AI's builders can't finance their data centers, the memory inside them gets harder to sell.

At 12:45 p.m. ET, Elon Musk replied to a Zerohedge post on X:

"For sure in 2027, but if China ramps LP5 & LP6 as fast as they've ramped other manufactured products, then 2028 will be a different story. HBM is a tougher hill to climb, however."

HBM Is the Tougher Hill

So Musk's warning is about low-power DRAM, and about 2028. CXMT's own plan fits it: its first 4F² product is standard server memory.

That matters, since SK hynix's margins depend on tight supply. Its gross margin went from under 1% in the September 2023 quarter to 79% in the March 2026 quarter. Second-quarter revenue jumped 257% to KRW 79.3 trillion, with a 76% operating margin, and management expects supply to stay tight for a long time.

The 2023 low is the warning: when supply loosens, memory margins can collapse fast.

Priced for a Downturn
SKHY NTM P/E: 5-Year (TIKR)

SK hynix sits 28.5% below its 52-week high. Its Seoul shares trade at 3.12x forward normalized earnings, barely above their 2026 low of 3.10x and less than half their five-year average of 6.94x (an average distorted by the 2022–2023 memory downturn, when forward earnings turned negative). On the US shares, Monday's $142.87 close works out to about 4.1x the 2027 EPS estimate below.

SKHY Normalized EPS Consensus Estimates (TIKR)

Analysts still expect normalized EPS to climb from $26.68 in fiscal 2026 to $34.48 in 2027 and $44.63 in 2028.

Musk was talking about Chinese supply, not SK hynix's earnings. But if his 2028 warning plays out, that year's estimate is the most exposed, and only three analysts make it.

Analysts' mean price target was still $252 midweek, about 76% above Monday's close.

Oct. 28 Is the Real Test

SK hynix holds its third-quarter call at 9 a.m. Seoul time on Oct. 28 (8 p.m. ET on Oct. 27). Listen for firm customer commitments for 2027, and for any word on the HBM4 equipment report.

My take: at 3x to 4x forward earnings, SK hynix looks like a buy. The price already assumes the boom ends, and Musk sees HBM, where SK hynix leads, as China's tougher hill.

Of course, if memory prices roll over, those earnings shrink, and neither multiple will look cheap anymore.

Reports that OpenAI (NASDAQ:OAI) is seeking approximately $30 billion in fresh funding ahead of rival Anthropic's (NASDAQ:ANTP) anticipated stock market debut added another focus for investors evaluating the scale and financing of AI investment.

Why US Stock Markets Are in Focus

Investing.com - U.S. stock market futures float around the flatline, as investors prepared for an accelerating flood of corporate results and gauged the outlook for the artificial intelligence trade. Netflix and United Airlines are among the highlights of the quarterly earnings agenda, while OpenAI is reportedly racing to raise $30 billion ahead of Anthropic's much-anticipated initial public offering.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

1. Futures mixed

U.S. stock futures were mixed on Tuesday. By 03:17 ET (07:17 GMT), the Dow futures contract had risen by 163 points, or 0.3%, S&P 500 futures had ticked up by 7 points, or 0.1%, and Nasdaq 100 futures had fallen by 62 points, or 0.2%.

The main averages on Wall Street finished around both sides of the flatline in the prior session. The benchmark S&P 500 gained 0.41% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.11%, while the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average edged down by 0.07%.

Tech stocks were among the standout performers, with the Nasdaq notching its best day in two weeks and a tracker of the chip industry breaking an eight-session run of declines. Given the concentration of tech in the broader index, this helped lift the S&P despite a pullback in almost two-thirds of the components within the average, analysts at Deutsche Bank said.

AI names, in particular, stabilized after a selloff driven by concerns over debt-driven spending and elevated borrowing costs. However, the AI trade reversed course once again this morning, dragging down the KOSPI in South Korea and the Nikkei in Japan.

2. Oil prices climb

Elsewhere, oil prices jumped, leaving benchmark Brent crude futures last exchanging hands above $110 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures have also increased by over 1% to $105.02 a barrel.

Brent settled within touching distance of a five-month high on Monday, even though it had fallen earlier in the session on reports that the U.S. and Iran may have reached a breakthrough in mediated negotiations.

However, that decline had a short shelf life. Oil prices surged once again after Iran's First Vice President said the country had "no choice but to exercise sovereignty" over the Strait of Hormuz, exacerbating worries over crude supply disruptions in the critical chokepoint.

Recent strikes on vessels near Hormuz have slowed the flow of oil through the waterway. Hormuz has been largely shuttered since after the start of a joint U.S.-Israeli assault on Iran in late February, although reported shipping figures have indicated that supplies showed signs of recovery last month.

3. Netflix to report

Meanwhile, Netflix is due to report after the close on Tuesday.

Last week, the streaming titan reportedly said it planned to slash around 6% of its workforce, or roughly 1,000 roles. The jobs impacted would mostly be in the firm's product, legal, tech and human-resources units, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

It was the biggest round of job reductions at the company since 2022. At the end of last year, Netflix employed about 16,000 workers.

The move comes as Netflix is grappling with easing customer engagement after years of strong growth that put intense pressure on traditional cable television businesses. A failed bid to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery's streaming and studio assets earlier this year has also exacerbated concerns around the group's overall strategy.

4. United Airlines earnings ahead

United Airlines is also scheduled to report after the close of U.S. markets.

Investors will likely be keeping tabs on United's pricing strategy for fares during a time when the wider airline industry has been grappling with increased fuel expenses.

In August, CEO Scott Kirby said he expects airfares to edge up gradually in the first half of next year, thanks in part to solid travel demand. But Kirby predicted that the increase would not be "as big a jump as happened this year."

"There really hasn't even been a blip in demand," Kirby told reporters at the time.

He also noted that United has not seen a slowdown in customer appetite for travel, adding that this strength may help to offset the elevated fuel costs.

Tuesday's earnings agenda will also feature returns from aerospace and defense sector names GE Aerospace and RTX Corporation, as well as carmaker General Motors. Elon Musk's SpaceX will also report after the closing bell.

5. OpenAI races to raise $30 billion ahead of Anthropic IPO - Reuters

OpenAI is accelerating fundraising to secure investor commitments before rival Anthropic's expected mid-November stock market debut, in a push that could value the ChatGPT maker at more than $1.4 trillion, according to Reuters.

Citing people familiar with the matter, Reuters reported that OpenAI is seeking about $30 billion from investors, including existing backers SoftBank Group and Abu Dhabi-based MGX. Both OpenAI and Anthropic, the firms behind the popular chatbots ChatGPT and Claude, respectively, are competing for capital from sovereign wealth funds and major institutional investors ahead of massive potential public flotations.

OpenAI is pitching investors on annualized revenue of $50 billion, Reuters reported, adding that the company expects the top-line number to reach $70 billion by the end of the year following the launch of its GPT-6 Astra model.

Anthropic's quarterly revenue reportedly rose to $16.8 billion in the third quarter, up from $11.6 billion in the prior three-month period. However, slower sequential revenue growth has raised questions about its valuation.
